paper_a.title: Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space (Mikolov et al., 2013)

paper_b.title: GloVe: Global Vectors for Word Representation (Pennington, Socher, Manning, 2014)

metadata.description: Word2Vec and GloVe are concurrent/near-simultaneous approaches to learning dense word embeddings that capture semantic relationships. Both learn vectors where linear algebraic operations reflect semantic analogies. Word2vec uses local context prediction (CBOW/Skip-gram) via SGD; GloVe uses explicit factorization of the global co-occurrence matrix via weighted least squares. Levy & Goldberg (2014) showed Skip-gram implicitly factorizes a shifted PMI matrix, revealing the methods are more similar than they appear.

matches.explanation: Both produce distributed word vectors $\mathbf{w} \in \mathbb{R}^d$ where semantic similarity is captured by geometric proximity (cosine similarity). The output representation is functionally identical: a lookup table mapping words to dense vectors.

Both define training objectives over word co-occurrence information, but through different lenses. Skip-gram: predict context words from center word via softmax (local, online). GloVe: minimize weighted squared error between dot product and log co-occurrence count (global, batch). Levy & Goldberg showed Skip-gram with negative sampling implicitly optimizes $\mathbf{w}_i^T \tilde{\mathbf{w}}_j \approx \mathrm{PMI}(i,j) - \log k$, which is closely related to GloVe's $\mathbf{w}_i^T \tilde{\mathbf{w}}_j \approx \log X_{ij}$.
CBOW (predicting center word from context average) has no direct GloVe counterpart. GloVe is inherently symmetric in its treatment of word and context.
Hierarchical softmax is a word2vec-specific approximation to the full softmax. GloVe does not need softmax at all since it optimizes a regression objective.

GloVe's explicit construction and analysis of the word co-occurrence matrix $X_{ij}$ and co-occurrence probability ratios $P_{ik}/P_{jk}$ is specific to GloVe. Word2vec works with raw text directly, never constructing a co-occurrence matrix.
GloVe's theoretical motivation via co-occurrence probability ratios (showing that ratios encode semantic relationships) is unique to GloVe and provides a principled derivation of the objective.

Both evaluate on the same word analogy task (semantic and syntactic analogies via vector arithmetic $\mathbf{v}_b - \mathbf{v}_a + \mathbf{v}_c \approx \mathbf{v}_d$) and achieve comparable performance. This shared evaluation framework demonstrates both methods learn equivalent linear structure.
Word2vec's King-Queen analogy example became iconic. GloVe reproduces similar examples but does not introduce new analogy paradigms.

Both discuss scalability but from different perspectives. Word2vec emphasizes fast training on billion-word corpora via online SGD. GloVe emphasizes that global co-occurrence statistics are more statistically efficient than local windows, requiring fewer passes over data.
